officialTitle: Amivantamab plus chemotherapy with and without lazertinib in EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC after disease progression on osimertinib: primary results from the phase III MARIPOSA-2 study

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 657 patients with EGFR-mutated (exon 19 deletions or L858R) locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC after disease progression on osimertinib were randomized 2 : 2 : 1
design.notes: Lazertinib schedule in the triplet arm was modified mid-study (start after carboplatin completion) because of haematologic toxicity.

clinicalQuestion: After progression on osimertinib, does adding amivantamab (with or without lazertinib) to carboplatin-pemetrexed improve PFS over chemotherapy alone?

pico.population: EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with disease progression on osimertinib
pico.intervention: Amivantamab plus carboplatin-pemetrexed, or amivantamab-lazertinib plus carboplatin-pemetrexed
pico.outcomes: Dual primary: PFS for each amivantamab arm vs chemotherapy. Others: ORR, intracranial PFS, safety

publications.title: Amivantamab plus chemotherapy with and without lazertinib in EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC after disease progression on osimertinib: primary results from the phase III MARIPOSA-2 study.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: PFS was significantly longer for amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy versus chemotherapy [hazard ratio (HR) for disease progression or death 0.48 and 0.44, respectively; P < 0.001 for both; median of 6.3 and 8.3 versus 4.2 months, respectively].

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: PFS was significantly longer for amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy versus chemotherapy [hazard ratio (HR) for disease progression or death 0.48 and 0.44, respectively; P < 0.001 for both; median of 6.3 and 8.3 versus 4.2 months, respectively].
Objective response rate was significantly higher for amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy versus chemotherapy (64% and 63% versus 36%, respectively; P < 0.001 for both).

Median intracranial PFS was 12.5 and 12.8 versus 8.3 months for amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy versus chemotherapy (HR for intracranial disease progression or death 0.55 and 0.58, respectively).

safety.description: Predominant adverse events with amivantamab-containing regimens
safety.sourceQuote: Predominant adverse events (AEs) in the amivantamab-containing regimens were hematologic, EGFR-, and MET-related toxicities. Amivantamab-chemotherapy had lower rates of hematologic AEs than amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy.

strengths: Randomised phase III in a post-osimertinib population with limited options
BICR primary endpoint with consistent investigator-assessed results
limitations: Mid-study regimen modification of the triplet arm

clinicalImplications.text: Supports amivantamab plus carboplatin-pemetrexed as a post-osimertinib option for EGFR-mutant NSCLC, including improved intracranial disease control.

tumourBoardPearl.text: After osimertinib failure, the amivantamab-chemotherapy doublet delivered the PFS gain with less haematologic toxicity than the lazertinib-containing triplet.
